q7.answer: Workers read `billing_mode` from the config service and, if it is unreadable, keep their last known mode. I did not design a push or propagation mechanism or say what happens to an invoice being processed at the moment of change. The only protection I specified is that the idempotency key (customer, billing_period) in the payment provider and ledger prevents double charges when workers briefly disagree.

q8.answer: Evidence is computed from the shadow store and comparison results, not stored as a count, and gate and sign-off decisions are recorded with who and when. What stops early promotion is that a person makes each move after checking that the gate is met. I did not specify a hard technical block that rejects a flag change when the gate is unmet, so that enforcement is not decided.

q9.answer: I did not name a specific component. I said the automatic rollback triggers when the new engine's charge failure rate exceeds 2% in any 10-minute window in `both` or `new_only`, that it starts at RB1 and pages on-call, and that it is ignored if a rollback is already running. Which service measures it was not decided.

q10.answer: At RB1 the rollback record is opened and the new engine starts no new charges, while in-flight calls finish. Charges that fall due are delayed, not lost. They are made at RB4, when the old engine charges each due period that has no ledger charge, using the idempotency key and skipping periods already in the ledger. After RB5 verifies exactly one charge per due period, the flag flips to `old_only`.

q11.answer: Two layers: both engines send the idempotency key (customer, billing_period) to the payment provider, and the ledger enforces uniqueness on the same key. RB2 reconciles unknown-outcome charges by looking them up by key, and RB4 skips periods already in the ledger, whichever engine charged them. RB5 then verifies exactly one charge per due period.

q12.answer: The rollback goes to `rb_blocked`. The fence stays on, so the new engine does not charge, the flag does not flip, and on-call is paged. On-call fixes the cause and retries from RB2, which is safe because charges are idempotent. There is no automatic exit or abort, and whether to add an abort action is an open question.
